# Results — Study 511 (Volume-Momentum, Lee-Swaminathan)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **trading
volume conditions momentum: high-volume winners and low-volume losers drive the drift, and
high-volume performers reverse faster** (Lee & Swaminathan 2000) — tested as a monthly
cross-sectional double-sort on a fixed **40-name large-cap survivor basket**. We form the 12-1
momentum signal and a trailing **dollar-volume** (turnover) measure, split the cross-section at
its median turnover into a HIGH-volume and a LOW-volume half, build a winners-minus-losers (WML)
book inside each, and ask whether the Lee-Swaminathan ordering holds, survives costs, and shows
the predicted faster reversal. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python
examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes **+ dollar volume** (close × share volume) — 40 long-listed US large-caps (public, no key) |
| Window | 2013-01-02 → 2025-12-30 (**13.0** years; price tape 3,269 days, 156 month-ends) |
| Basket | fixed 40-name large-cap **survivor** panel (same family as [507](../../507-cross-sectional-momentum/) / [510](../../510-frog-in-the-pan/)) |
| Signal | 12-1 momentum (12-month trailing return, skip the most recent month) |
| Conditioner | trailing mean daily **dollar volume** over the same 12-1 formation window; median split → HIGH / LOW volume halves |
| Book | inside each volume half: long top 30% / short bottom 30% by momentum, equal-weight, dollar-neutral |
| Lag / costs | form on month-end *m*, enter the **next** session, hold month *m+1* (one forward lag, no look-ahead); **5 bps** one-way × NAV × turnover + **50 bps/yr** borrow on the short leg |
| Fingerprints | prices `99db07758961` · volume `ef22b095227e` |
| As-of | 2026-06-26 |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 40 names *still trading* in 2026.
> A momentum loser leg's natural shorts — firms that trended down into delisting/bankruptcy — are
> absent by construction. In the Lee-Swaminathan world the **low-volume losers** are precisely the
> *quiet* names that fade into delisting, so the volume-conditioned slice carries this bias too:
> any apparent premium is an **upper bound**. Opt-in guard: pass a delisting-complete panel to
> `strategy.long_short` to lift the bias; we cannot from yfinance, so we flag it.

## The signal — momentum WML inside each volume half

One forward execution lag; equal-weight dollar-neutral WML (top-30% − bottom-30% by 12-1
momentum) inside each turnover half. The HAC *t* is a Newey-West *t* of the monthly WML mean
against 0.

| book | n months | mean (ann) | vol (ann) | Sharpe | HAC *t* | hit-rate | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Plain momentum (no split) | 143 | +1.57% | 14.5% | +0.11 | +0.38 | 52% | −30% |
| **HIGH-volume WML** | 143 | **+2.53%** | 18.1% | +0.14 | **+0.44** | 50% | −39% |
| **LOW-volume WML** | 143 | **+4.55%** | 15.4% | +0.30 | **+1.26** | 50% | −31% |

Read it carefully. **Nothing clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** — the strongest book (LOW-volume WML)
reaches only HAC *t* = 1.26. And the Lee-Swaminathan ordering is **inverted on this tape**: the
literature predicts the **HIGH-volume** WML should be the larger, but here the **LOW-volume** WML
(+4.55%/yr) beats the HIGH-volume WML (+2.53%/yr). The famous "momentum life cycle" does not
appear in this large-cap survivor cross-section.

## The Lee-Swaminathan interaction — the headline ordering, signed

The interaction is the **HIGH-volume WML minus the LOW-volume WML**, month by month — predicted
*positive* by Lee & Swaminathan.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| N months | 143 |
| Mean (ann) | **−2.02%/yr** |
| HAC *t* | **−0.37** |
| Hit-rate | 48% |

The interaction is **negative and insignificant** — the *opposite sign* to the prediction, with
|*t*| well under 2. On this basket, conditioning momentum on volume does not concentrate it in the
high-volume names; if anything the quiet names carry the (still-insignificant) drift.

## Costs — the thin spread net of turnover + borrow

We charge **5 bps one-way × NAV × turnover** at each monthly rebalance plus **50 bps/yr** borrow
on the short (loser) leg, on the HIGH-volume book (the literature's strongest slice).

| HIGH-volume WML | mean (ann) | HAC *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| gross | +2.53% | +0.44 | +0.14 |
| **net of costs + borrow** | **+1.76%** | **+0.31** | +0.10 |

Avg monthly turnover **22%**, avg **6** names/leg. Net of costs the HIGH-volume book is +1.76%/yr
at HAC *t* = 0.31 — **statistically indistinguishable from zero** before *and* after costs. There
is no edge for costs to erode; the trade is a coin flip on a six-name leg.

## Robustness — the placebo null (seed-robust)

A **label-shuffle placebo**: inside the HIGH-volume half each month, shuffle which stock the
momentum signal points at (destroying genuine winner/loser persistence, preserving the volume
conditioning and leg sizes), recompute the WML mean, and report the share of shuffles whose mean
beats the real mean.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| Real mean (ann) | +2.53%/yr |
| Placebo mean (ann) | −0.07%/yr |
| Permutation *p* | **0.256** |

Seed-robustness (5 seeds, 400 perms each): *p* = **0.223 · 0.245 · 0.250 · 0.260 · 0.223** — a
stable ~0.24. About a quarter of random sorts of the same returns beat the observed WML; the
signal does **not** survive the null. (Not a lucky-seed artefact — the *p* is flat across seeds.)

## Third axis — the volume-conditioned reversal (the "momentum life cycle")

Lee-Swaminathan's sharpest prediction: **high-volume** performers *reverse faster*, so the
HIGH-volume WML's cumulative drift should fade (or turn negative) at longer holds sooner than the
LOW-volume book's. We build the WML inside each half at growing holds (1 / 3 / 6 / 12 months) and
report the **cumulative** WML over the hold and its HAC *t*.

| hold (months) | HIGH-vol cum WML | HIGH-vol *t* | LOW-vol cum WML | LOW-vol *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | +0.21% | +0.44 | +0.38% | +1.26 |
| 3 | +0.38% | +0.27 | +0.83% | +1.12 |
| 6 | +1.16% | +0.42 | +1.36% | +1.02 |
| 12 | +2.15% | +0.48 | +4.20% | +1.58 |

The predicted faster high-volume reversal **does not appear**: neither book reverses (both drift
mildly *up* with the hold, none significantly), and the LOW-volume book leads the HIGH-volume book
at every horizon — the reverse of the life-cycle claim. The "momentum life cycle" is **busted** on
this tape.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic panel where a known momentum drift is **concentrated in the high-turnover names**
(`vol_tilt = 0.8`). The engine must score ~0 on both slices at zero strength, and at positive
strength recover a **bigger HIGH-volume WML than LOW-volume WML** (positive interaction).

| planted strength | HIGH-vol mean (ann) | HIGH-vol *t* | LOW-vol mean (ann) | LOW-vol *t* | interaction gap |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | −1.2% | −0.28 | +1.1% | +0.18 | −2.3% |
| 0.20 | +27.3% | +3.67 | +7.9% | +1.30 | **+19.3%** |
| 0.40 | +65.4% | +7.87 | +36.2% | +4.88 | **+29.2%** |
| 0.60 | +106.8% | +10.62 | +68.1% | +8.00 | **+38.7%** |

With **no** planted edge the interaction sits at ≈0 (no false positive — noise cannot fake the
ordering); with a planted volume-tilted drift the HIGH-volume WML lights up and **exceeds** the
LOW-volume WML monotonically, exactly the Lee-Swaminathan pattern. The measurement is unbiased —
so the real-tape result (HIGH-volume WML *t* = 0.44, **negative** interaction) is a genuine
*absence* of the effect on large-cap survivors, not a construction artefact.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The HIGH-volume WML earns +2.53%/yr at HAC *t* = **0.44**; the LOW-volume WML
  +4.55%/yr at *t* = **1.26** — the strongest book is still under the *t* ≥ 2 bar. The
  Lee-Swaminathan **interaction is negative** (−2.02%/yr, *t* = −0.37): the *opposite sign* to the
  prediction. A seed-robust label-shuffle placebo gives *p* ≈ **0.24**. Nothing certifies.
  Survivorship is named on this axis — and it only *inflates* the numbers, so the real broad-universe
  result is, if anything, weaker.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of 5 bps/leg × turnover + 50 bps/yr borrow, the HIGH-volume book
  is **+1.76%/yr at HAC *t* = 0.31** — indistinguishable from zero before and after costs, on a
  six-name leg of a 40-name survivor basket. There is no spread to trade.
- **"Momentum life cycle — high volume reverses faster"? — BUSTED.** The double-sort ordering is
  inverted (LOW-volume WML > HIGH-volume WML at every horizon), and the predicted faster
  high-volume reversal never shows: both books drift mildly up with the hold, neither reverses,
  none is significant. The synthetic control proves the engine *would* find the pattern if it were
  there — it isn't, on this large-cap survivor tape.
